title: Restriction on raw cohomology of a fixed injective resolution
statement: Let $Z$ be a scheme, $F$ an $\mathcal O_Z$-module, $I$ a nonnegative injective resolution of $F$, $U\subseteq Z$ open, and $R$ a RestrictedResolutionSections identification of $I|_U$ as in [def-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-open-choices]. For $p\in\mathbf N$, write $c_I:H^p(Z,F)\longrightarrow H^p(I(Z))$ and $c_R:H^p(U,F|_U)\longrightarrow H^p(R.resolution(U))$ for the global sections resolution comparisons, with the forgetful homology comparison as in [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift]. Let $r:I(Z)\to I(U)$ be degreewise section restriction and let $a=R.sections:R.resolution(U)\simeq I(U)$. Then $H^p(a)\circ c_R\circ res^Z_U=H^p(r)\circ c_I$, where $res^Z_U$ is [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]. This is equality of additive group morphisms before any section-class map to a homology sheaf.

source.place: Equation 20.7.1.1 (01E2) and its construction in Lemma 20.7.1 (01E1); Remark 20.14.2 (01FB), augmented-lift calculation

proof.text: Restriction preserves finite limits; its right adjoint, direct image along the open inclusion, therefore preserves injectives. The pushforward of the chosen restricted resolution is already a termwise injective complex.

Compose the restriction-unit complex map with the pushforward of R.comparison.inv. Naturality of the unit and the augmentation equation show it is an augmented lift. Use source resolution I, target resolution R.resolution, this lift as beta, and lambda the identity as ModuleCohomologyFMapData. The canonical comparison of global sections is an isomorphism, so the homology invertibility field follows by functoriality.

Independence of ModuleCohomologyFMapData identifies the map computed with these choices with moduleCohomologyRestriction. In each degree, naturality of R.comparison.inv commutes the top-open correction past it. Cancel comparison.inv with comparison.hom. R.components and the restriction-unit formula then leave exactly the top-to-U restriction of sections.

Apply the homology functor to that complex identity. The inverse target resolution comparison cancels the target resolution comparison, and the inverse of the homology map of the global sections isomorphism is its mapped inverse. Functoriality gives the displayed equality. The same inverse identities hold for empty and top opens, zero modules, and p=0.

proof_origin.place: Specialization of Remark 20.14.2 to restriction along an open inclusion; direct image preserves injectives, so lambda is the identity.

theorem restrictedResolution_cohomology {Z : Scheme.{u}} {F : Z.Modules}
    (I : InjectiveResolution F) (U : Z.Opens) (R : RestrictedResolutionSections I U)
    (p : ℕ) :
    let := RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor_additive Z.toRingedSpace
    let := RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor_additive U.toScheme.toRingedSpace
    moduleCohomologyRestriction U F p ≫
      (forget₂ _ AddCommGrpCat.{u}).map
        (R.resolution.isoRightDerivedObj
          (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor U.toScheme.toRingedSpace) p).hom ≫
      (((RingedSpace.globalSectionsComplex R.resolution).sc p).mapHomologyIso
        (forget₂ _ AddCommGrpCat.{u})).inv ≫
      (HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (ComplexShape.up ℕ) p).map
        R.sections.hom =
    (forget₂ _ AddCommGrpCat.{u}).map
      (I.isoRightDerivedObj (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor Z.toRingedSpace) p).hom ≫
      (((RingedSpace.globalSectionsComplex I).sc p).mapHomologyIso
        (forget₂ _ AddCommGrpCat.{u})).inv ≫
      (HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (ComplexShape.up ℕ) p).map
        ((NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex
          (Functor.whiskerLeft (SheafOfModules.forget Z.ringCatSheaf ⋙
            PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf Z.ringCatSheaf.obj)
              ((evaluation Z.Opensᵒᵖ AddCommGrpCat.{u}).map
                (homOfLE (show U ≤ ⊤ from le_top)).op))
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).app I.cocomplex)
